find: On the outside of the bag, mark the water line with the marker.
replace: Hold the bag flat against the sunny window where it will hang, and mark the water line on the outside with a permanent marker.
why: A line marked before taping moves about 1 cm, more than the bag's real change; washable ink beads on plastic.

find: inside a clear zip bag with a little warm water at the bottom, keeping the cup upright and its outside above the water
replace: upright inside one large clear zip bag together with Cup B and a damp paper towel at room temperature (warm water fogs the bag itself; open it briefly for the wipe)
why: Warm water fogs the bag walls and hides Cup A; Cup B inside keeps the comparison fair.

find: upright inside a clear zip bag with a little warm water at the bottom, keeping the outside of the cup above the water
replace: upright inside one large clear zip bag together with Cup B and a damp paper towel at room temperature (warm water fogs the bag itself; open it briefly for the wipe)
why: Same fix in the speaker notes.

find: Which setup will let them compare the water level with its starting level later?
replace: Which setup makes the sealed model and lets them compare the water level with its starting level later?
why: As worded an open bag also works.

find: Observations that support Ben’s explanation: droplets formed on cold Cup A, Cup B stayed dry, and droplets returned after wiping.
replace: The observation that decides it: Cup B also holds water but stayed dry, so water does not leak through cup walls. Droplets forming and coming back after wiping would happen under Ana’s idea too.
why: Only Cup B tells the two ideas apart.

find: Evidence that supports Ben: droplets formed on cold Cup A, Cup B stayed dry, and droplets returned after wiping.
replace: The observation that decides it: Cup B also holds water but stayed dry, so water does not leak through cup walls. Droplets forming and coming back after wiping would happen under Ana’s idea too.
why: The line the teacher says aloud.

find: Also accept: I think Ben is right because I saw droplets return after the outside of Cup A was wiped dry.
replace: Also accept: I think Ben is right because I saw that Cup B has water in it too but stayed dry. A reason citing only the wiped patch fits Ana’s idea too; ask what Cup B would show if water leaked.
why: Full credit was given for evidence that does not decide.

find: Leave an air space above the water.
replace: Leave an air space above the water, so water vapor has room to collect and drops can form on the bag.
why: The quiz grades this reason and nothing taught it.

find: Start the ice water cup now so droplets have time to form.
replace: Start the ice water cup now so droplets have time to form, but keep both cups behind a folder until students have written their predictions.
why: Otherwise students predict with droplets already visible.

find: suppose a pitcher of lemonade sits on a patio table
replace: suppose a pitcher of ice-cold lemonade sits on a patio table
why: As written, humid air alone makes it sweat: the misconception.

find: For you only: the diagram and paragraph count 70% of the course grade and the lesson quizzes 30%. Do not show this to students.
replace: The diagram and paragraph count 70% of the course grade and the lesson quizzes 30%.
why: A writer's rule leaked as a secrecy order; lesson 2 announces the 30%.

find: a short quiz closes the lesson.
replace: a short quiz closes the lesson. Several days before, set a marked pair of cups in the sunny window and the shady cupboard, and check that the lamp warms things (an LED lamp barely does).
